gloss: morning person; day person; having a daytime-oriented lifestyle

definitions.explanation: A person whose natural rhythm is geared toward the daytime — getting up early, being most productive in the morning and afternoon, and going to bed at a reasonable hour. Also the lifestyle pattern itself. Typically contrasted with {夜型|よるがた} (night person).

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}は{昼型|ひるがた}だ。
{昼型|ひるがた}の{生活|せいかつ}に{切|き}り{替|か}えたい。
examples.english: I want to switch to a daytime-oriented lifestyle.

examples.japanese: {夜型|よるがた}だった{彼|かれ}も、{子|こ}どもが{生|う}まれてからは{昼型|ひるがた}になった。
examples.english: He used to be a night owl, but after his child was born he became a day person.

notes:
Composed of {昼|ひる} ("daytime") + {型|がた} ("type, pattern"). The {〜型|がた} suffix forms "type" nouns: {血液型|けつえきがた} (blood type), {新型|しんがた} (new type/model), {大型|おおがた} (large-type).

USAGE:
- Used both attributively ({昼型|ひるがた}の{人|ひと}, {昼型|ひるがた}の{生活|せいかつ}) and predicatively ({彼|かれ}は{昼型|ひるがた}だ).
- Frequently paired with {夜型|よるがた} in health and lifestyle discussions.
- Appears in topics like sleep hygiene, work-from-home routines, and chronotype science — lining up roughly with the English notions of "early bird" vs. "night owl."
- Changing from {夜型|よるがた} to {昼型|ひるがた} (or the reverse) is typically described with verbs like {変|か}える, {切|き}り{替|か}える (to switch), or {直|なお}す (to fix).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {昼型|ひるがた}の{生活|せいかつ}: a daytime-oriented lifestyle
- {昼型|ひるがた}の{人|ひと}: a day person
- {昼型|ひるがた}に{なる|なる}: to become a day person
- {昼型|ひるがた}に{変|か}える / {切|き}り{替|か}える: to switch to a daytime schedule
- {昼型|ひるがた}{生活|せいかつ}を{送|おく}る: to lead a daytime-oriented life

ANTONYM:
- {夜型|よるがた}: night person, night-oriented — someone who is alert and productive late at night and sleeps late in the morning.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {朝型|あさがた}: morning person / morning-oriented — a near-synonym, emphasizing the early-morning pattern specifically; often preferred over {昼型|ひるがた} in some regions and writings.
